title: Architecture
content:
next adds a real automatic semantic builder while preserving the v0.1 authority boundary:

public-document allow-list
  → durable source inventory
  → evidence extraction
  → optional complete evidence batching
  → Agent semantic proposal
  → deterministic validation
  → KnowledgeRevision
  ├→ human-review graph
  └→ CognitivePackageDraft → candidate handoff → A3S Use generation

Domain model {#domain-model}

Workspace, KnowledgeScope, ScopeLifecycle, ScopeInventory, Evidence, SemanticProposal, KnowledgeRevision, and CognitivePackageDraft keep separate responsibilities. ScopeLifecycle gates source reads; a separate Workspace-wide KnowledgeRevisionHead owns ontology activation. Source observations reconcile by aggregate sequence into immutable versions or removal tombstones, and every build freezes one complete inventory snapshot plus the exact versions of its explicit sources before admission.

M6 now includes explicit opt-in exact HTTPS + HTML admission. A scope must list each canonical, credential-free port-443 URL without query or fragment and allow text/html; the application must also inject the resolver, and HTML links never expand the source set. Every hop uses a bounded all-public DNS set pinned into its TLS request, with environment proxies and automatic redirects disabled and at most three same-authority redirects. Private, reserved, or mixed addresses, cross-origin or looping redirects, media, header, content-coding, or inventory drift, empty or oversized responses, timeout, and cancellation all fail before parsing.

The HTML parser is html-semantic@v1+scraper-0.22.0. It excludes script, style, template, hidden, SVG, and canvas subtrees and emits stable DOM locators for headings, paragraphs, lists, code, quotes, and tables. Bytes, markup, DOM nodes, depth, blocks, and text have hard ceilings; malformed HTML must still pass them after deterministic recovery. The bundled CLI remains local-file-only.

M6 also implements an exact-revision Git tree library adapter. Scope binds an exact repository ID, complete non-zero lowercase SHA-1/SHA-256 commit OID, and optional path prefix; each source additionally binds its raw blob OID, portable path, and regular/executable mode. The caller must explicitly supply the local object database, Git executable, and digest-bound ignore/limit policy. The adapter never clones, fetches, checks out, resolves a branch/tag/abbreviated revision, reads worktree bytes, or interprets repository .gitignore, attributes, filters, or LFS. Alternates, common directories, config includes, object links, symlink/submodule entries, non-UTF-8 or non-portable paths, and case collisions fail closed. Git output, tree, blob, object layout, elapsed time, and cancellation are bounded, while commit/blob hashes and frozen inventory are rechecked before parsing. The CLI still does not configure this adapter.

The build-time evidence-discovery port for large corpora is also implemented. Its request binds the project, complete EvidenceIndex digest, every source/document/Parser/block/locator/excerpt identity, and hard item, text, batch, and elapsed-time limits. A lexical or embedding implementation may return only a complete Evidence ID partition: every admitted ID exactly once. Unknown, missing, duplicate, oversized, late, cancelled, or index/policy-identity-drifted plans fail before a model call, after which the learner still resolves original evidence from the authoritative EvidenceIndex. The built-in LexicalEvidenceIndex deterministically supports Chinese and Latin-script terms. The CLI keeps canonical ID order by default and enables it only with --evidence-index lexical. The port has no source, graph, package, approval, or Agent-session authority.

After exact human approval, the engine deterministically compiles or reuses an immutable revision. It retains grounded claims, concepts, procedures, conflicts, and excerpt-free evidence identities; package-only Skill guidance is not ontology authority. The store records the complete source → document → evidence → revision → revision-bound draft dependency chain before exact-parent compare-and-swap activation. Object-first publication, replay stability, and closed corruption checks prevent partial or competing active heads.

Activation reconciliation revalidates the exact revision and original approved material into a non-deserializable package input. The A3S compiler reads ontology semantics only from that revision and writes the revision, semantic digest, and both compiler generations into package provenance and the final digest; Skill, blueprint, supplied artifacts, and permitted excerpts remain bound to the approval.

The internal graph writer is now implemented. It deterministically builds human-review-only nodes, edges, and sequence events from the exact revision, then appends revision → projection revocation lineage after durable storage. Evidence nodes carry opaque IDs only, and Agent access is fixed off. An independent disclosure presenter now reconstructs the minimum public graph from allow-listed bilingual documents, so internal semantic copy never enters the static site directly.

The A3S Use boundary can now emit an immutable candidate handoff with no lifecycle state. A read-only observer rechecks the exact reviewed lock digest, complete dependency closure, one Registry snapshot, TUF catalogs, and enabled schema-v3 receipts before the generation writer may append draft → generation revocation lineage. It cannot resolve dependencies, install, mutate the Registry, or publish. Real A3S Use 0.3 host wiring, signed publication, rollback/revocation, and A3S Code session binding remain next work.

next also adds a closed reviewed Workflow candidate path. The learner may deterministically build ProcedureFlowPlan v2 from grounded, cited procedures only when the caller selected the workflow profile and set allow_flow_synthesis=true in policy before any model call. Resource content and model output cannot enable it. The source-free plan binds the exact blueprint, policy, complete cognition, selected procedures, OKF capability, planner generation, canonical source path and export, renderer generation, and raw source digest. The package graph must contain Skill → OKF, Skill → Flow, and Flow → OKF, and evaluation plus human approval bind that exact identity. Review and compilation independently reconstruct the same bounded TypeScript bytes.

This change advances the internal DraftCognitivePackage to schema v6; the A3S Use package manifest remains schema v3. A3sPackageCompiler emits the Flow source and a path-free readiness receipt only when the application injects an absolute compiler path, its exact SHA-256 digest, and an absolute cache root. It then calls real a3s-flow 0.11 native preflight and runs an exact preflight-mode offline harness. Missing configuration, compiler/source drift, compilation failure, protocol mismatch, or readiness drift blocks the whole candidate. Agentic Ontology does not discover, download, or distribute the native compiler, so provider/platform-qualified production readiness and publication remain open.

An approval-bound package candidate can now also project to deterministic tar+gzip with fixed file order, package/ root, paths, data/executable modes, uid/gid, mtime, and gzip header. A3S Use must re-admit the temporary archive to the exact same package and manifest identity as the directory. Optional hosted Skill v1 output contains only the generated SKILL.md; its A3S canonical descriptor binds bundle and entrypoint, direct capabilities, manifest, exact Git commit, approval operation, agent-input, and A3S Code/Use compatibility. Both outputs remain unsigned local candidates with no lifecycle authority. Registry, TUF, installation, locking, and publication still belong to A3S Use.

The evidence boundary pins Parser's generated capability matrix and preserves each admitted DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, or image row in provenance. Format, media type, natural unit, support-status, and matrix-digest drift fail before semantic projection. Release-grade provider and platform qualification remains open.

A separate release gate now pins the qualification policy and requires exact, independently reviewed receipt bytes with passed five-profile, provider, resume, Linux, macOS, and Windows evidence. Missing, failed, or unavailable evidence cannot become a release claim. No passing receipt is bundled today, so the current Parser boundary remains contract-qualified rather than release-qualified.

Model evidence uses prompt-contract v2. The digest binds fixed system, task, schema-metadata, and inert-envelope instructions; context and evidence carry byte counts and SHA-256 identities after framing delimiters are escaped. Locale tags cannot inject prompt lines, and closed proposal schemas reject Tool, permission, package, and approval fields.

After decoding, semantic IDs are reconstructed rather than trusted. Relationships require admitted evidence, while map-key drift, self or dangling edges, duplicate conflicts, and non-canonical bounded fields fail before evaluation.

Quality {#quality}

The real builder now carries active-scope denial, frozen inventory-to-build binding, exact HTTPS/HTML and exact-revision Git tree admission, complete-coverage build-time evidence discovery, deterministic revision digests, exact-parent activation receipts, an internal GraphProjection writer, revision dependency evidence, revision-bound package candidates, deterministic package archives, hosted Skill v1 bundles/descriptors, an A3S Use handoff, an authenticated generation-lineage writer, and default-off reviewed procedure Flow planning, rendering, preflight, and candidate compilation. The public presenter and disclosure regression gates are also implemented. Next completes cross-platform qualification for distribution artifacts and the native Flow compiler, adds signing/release automation, selects external embedding/model adapters from demonstrated demand, and wires the real lifecycle host, incremental-change receipts, and citation-coverage evaluation.

title: Agentic Ontology next documentation
content:
next records unreleased evolution. It is not evidence that a capability has shipped, production scale has been validated, or the real semantic builder is live.

Planned evolution

Add incremental changes and replayable build receipts above the disclosure projection implemented in v0.1.

Use the implemented exact-revision Git tree library adapter for caller-authorized local object databases; the current CLI remains local-file-only.

Use the implemented build-time evidence-discovery port and deterministic lexical index to batch large corpora; select an external embedding adapter only from demonstrated demand, without exposing retrieval to Agents.

Keep the public contract for learning events, graph nodes, relationships, and cognitive-package previews stable.

Connect a real A3S Use 0.3 host and signed lifecycle operations; the existing generation writer records lineage only from authoritative lock, TUF receipt, and Registry snapshot evidence without changing package state.

Add real citation coverage, package-generation diffs, and usage feedback to continual evaluation.

Keep source code and internal implementation out of public build artifacts.

The internal graph contains approved semantic copy and cannot be copied into the static site. v0.1 already reconstructs a minimum display contract from the public-document allow-list. next tightens evidence and receipts without broadening graph authority.

Use the version selector to return to v0.1 for the current public-build contract.

title: Playground
content:
v0.1 already uses an independent disclosure presenter to reconstruct a minimum public semantic contract from allow-listed bilingual documents; internal GraphProjection JSON is never copied into the site. next keeps the three linked regions—learning events, a human-review 3D ontology, and an A3S Use cognitive-package preview—and connects the six-stage build run to authoritative A3S Use and A3S Code receipts. Frontend state must never imply lifecycle success.

Compatibility requirements

Events continue to include time, public document, understood knowledge, created semantics, and target Revision.

Events continue to highlight graph nodes and relationships.

The package preview continues to show package schema, surfaces, revision, and publication state.

The keyboard semantic list continues to share filters, citations, and relationship data with the 3D graph; non-WebGL environments enter that list automatically.

The build run continues to show the objects, authorities, gates, and receipts for Scope, Evidence, Review, Revision, Package, and Evaluation.

When A3S Use or A3S Code has not issued a receipt, later stages remain waiting or blocked and never synthesize success.

Package contract {#package-contract}

The real builder must not add source-location fields, emit an Agent graph-query payload, or promote unverified Agent output directly into canonical knowledge.

title: Public data boundary
content:
The internal GraphProjection is not a public input. The current disclosure presenter reconstructs a minimum public graph from allow-listed public documents only. Its output passes closed-schema validation, dangerous-content scanning, a complete-artifact digest receipt, and static-file scanning. next must preserve or tighten these gates.

Required rejection

Any source code, code snippet, internal symbol, repository path, or line number;

Git metadata, source maps, local paths, and private network addresses;

generated material absent from public documentation that could be mistaken for a real product fact.

direct copies of internal claims, summaries, evidence references, or the complete projection JSON.

Any failed check prevents GitHub Pages artifact assembly.

title: Quick start
content:
next keeps Node.js 22, npm 11, and the same static build entry point:

npm install
npm run build

Use npm run dev for the product site, npm run dev:playground for the 3D Playground, and npm run dev:docs for versioned docs.

A new semantic builder must emit the current public contract and pass npm run check:public before its output can be assembled into GitHub Pages.

The Rust CLI batches evidence in canonical Evidence ID order by default. Add --evidence-index lexical explicitly only when a large corpus benefits from lexical acceleration; this changes build-time batching and never creates an Agent retrieval interface.

title: Versioning
content:
next uses /agentic-ontology/docs/next/; English uses /agentic-ontology/docs/next/en/. It always keeps a version prefix and never replaces the default v0.1 route.

Promoting a new default version requires Chinese/English page parity, public-graph contract compatibility, a passing privacy gate, Playground interaction regression coverage, and GitHub Pages route checks.
